title: When speech must answer at the Door
issueStatement: The mouth can become the place where greed, anger, slander, and self-praise try to look normal. Gurbani asks whether a word can stand with honor before the One who hears it.
centralInsight: The cited shabads do more than recommend politeness. They make speech a spiritual test: harshness brings grief, slander dirties the mouth, and remembrance becomes real when it sweetens the tongue and humbles the walk.
practicalReflection: Clean speech begins before technique. The heart has to stop enjoying the taste of injury, display, and control long enough for Naam to govern the next sentence.
actionPrompt: Before the next consequential sentence, ask whether it carries filth, ego, or honor; speak only what can stand at the Lord's Door.
